behavioral_notes.element: payment.transaction._send_payment_request / controllers.adyen_payments -> outbound POST to the Adyen Checkout API (/payments)
behavioral_notes.observation: The outbound acquirer call (gap #7) is centralized through payment's payment.provider._send_api_request, which payment_adyen targets at the Adyen Checkout API via _build_request_url. _build_request_url assembles 'https://{prefix}.adyen.com/checkout/V{version}/{endpoint}' in test mode and 'https://{prefix}-checkout-live.adyenpayments.com/checkout/V{version}/{endpoint}' in live mode, the prefix coming from adyen_api_url_prefix and the version from const.API_ENDPOINT_VERSIONS[endpoint]. _build_request_headers authenticates every call with an 'X-API-Key: <adyen_api_key>' header (key restricted to base.group_system) plus an 'idempotency-key' header on retryable POSTs. The merchant-initiated token charge (payment.transaction._send_payment_request) POSTs /payments with merchantAccount, minor-unit amount, the token's storedPaymentMethodId, shopperReference, recurringProcessingModel='Subscription' and shopperInteraction='ContAuth' for off-session recurring; the shopper-initiated front-end flow (controllers.adyen_payments) POSTs /payments with the live paymentMethod, 3DS authenticationData/browserInfo, storePaymentMethod=tx.tokenize and a returnUrl back to /payment/adyen/return. Both then call _process('adyen', response). captureDelayHours=0 is forced when the provider does not capture manually. None of this server-to-server HTTP is visible in Python field/model metadata.

Three public jsonrpc routes drive the Adyen Web drop-in. /payment/adyen/payment_methods POSTs /paymentMethods (sudo provider) to fetch the methods available for the amount/country/locale. /payment/adyen/payments first calls payment_utils.check_access_token to reject tampered amount/currency/partner data (else ValidationError), then POSTs /payments and _process()es the result. /payment/adyen/payments/details POSTs /payments/details to submit the result of an additional action (3DS challenge or redirect) and _process()es it. The HTTP /payment/adyen/return route (csrf=False, save_session=False) handles the redirect back from a 3DS1 page or redirect-only payment method: it _search_by_reference()es the tx by the merchantReference carried in the return URL, forces tx.operation='online_redirect', calls adyen_payment_details with the redirectResult, and redirects to /payment/status. This guarded check-token-then-charge sequencing and the cross-route 3DS handoff are invisible to metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: AdyenController.adyen_webhook (/payment/adyen/notification) -> HMAC signature verification + tx state update
behavioral_notes.observation: The public, csrf=False, POST-only webhook at /payment/adyen/notification parses data['notificationItems'][*]['NotificationRequestItem'], locates each tx via payment.transaction._search_by_reference, and calls _verify_signature BEFORE acting. _verify_signature reads additionalData.hmacSignature, recomputes the expected signature with _compute_signature (flatten the payload, pick the canonical key list pspReference/originalReference/merchantAccountCode/merchantReference/amount.value/amount.currency/eventCode/success, escape ':' and '\', join with ':', HMAC-SHA256 the signing string with the binary-decoded adyen_hmac_key, Base64-encode) and compares with hmac.compare_digest (constant-time), raising werkzeug Forbidden on mismatch or missing signature. On success it reshapes the notification (mapping eventCode AUTHORISATION/CANCELLATION/REFUND/CAPTURE/CAPTURE_FAILED + success flag into a resultCode) and calls tx_sudo._process('adyen', data), driving payment's guarded state machine via _apply_updates (_set_pending/_set_authorized/_set_done/_set_canceled/_set_error). The route always returns '[accepted]' to acknowledge. _search_by_reference also creates child transactions (_adyen_create_child_tx) for captures/voids/refunds initiated from the Adyen side. Signature trust, the constant-time compare, and the inbound state transition are all invisible to metadata.

When tx.tokenize is set, the shopper /payments request carries storePaymentMethod=True and recurringProcessingModel='CardOnFile'. After a successful authorisation, payment's engine calls _extract_token_values, which mines payment_data['additionalData']: it vaults a payment.token only if recurring.recurringDetailReference is present, storing provider_ref = the recurringDetailReference (Adyen stored-PM id), payment_details = additionalData.cardSummary (card last4), and adyen_shopper_reference = additionalData['recurring.shopperReference']. Subsequent merchant-initiated off-session charges (_send_payment_request) POST /payments with paymentMethod.storedPaymentMethodId=token.provider_ref, shopperReference=token.adyen_shopper_reference, recurringProcessingModel='Subscription', shopperInteraction='ContAuth'. _send_capture_request (POST /payments/{ref}/captures), _send_void_request (POST /payments/{ref}/cancels) and _send_refund_request (POST /payments/{ref}/refunds, negative amount) round out the authorize/capture/void/refund operations against the source provider_reference, each storing the new pspReference and re-using _process to fold the response into the state machine.

behavioral_notes.element: external integration surface (gap #7) -- endpoints, keys, SDK
behavioral_notes.observation: Static gap-#7 facts (extract_frontend.py): uses_api_keys=true; the single outbound endpoint family is 'https://{prefix_}.com/checkout/V{version}/{endpoint}' (the Adyen Checkout API, X-API-Key auth) -- resolved at runtime to {prefix}.adyen.com (test) or {prefix}-checkout-live.adyenpayments.com (live) -- declared in models/payment_provider.py. No 'requests' import here: HTTP is delegated to payment.provider._send_api_request in the parent engine, which payment_adyen configures via the _build_request_url / _build_request_headers / _parse_response_error hook overrides. On the browser side the Adyen Web Components/drop-in SDK (client_key) is loaded on pages showing the payment form -- a second, client-side channel to Adyen. This dual server-to-server + client-side acquirer link is the canonical metadata gap #7: none of it is reachable from model/field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) -- Adyen drop-in inline form patch
behavioral_notes.observation: 1 JS file, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds (gap #3). The module patches the shared PaymentForm widget (PaymentForm.prototype) rather than registering a new component: it consumes the inline-form values JSON from payment.provider._adyen_get_inline_form_values (client_key, the mapped Adyen payment-method code, the Adyen-formatted minor-unit amount) to mount the Adyen Web drop-in/Components, then drives the /payment/adyen/payment_methods, /payments and /payments/details jsonrpc routes to complete the charge and any 3DS additional action client-side. Assets load into web.assets_frontend (1 bundle entry). These browser interactions and the Adyen SDK are invisible to Python metadata (gap #3).

external_integrations.sdk: Adyen Web Components / drop-in (browser, client_key); server side uses no python SDK -- HTTP via payment.provider._send_api_request
external_integrations.auth: X-API-Key: <adyen_api_key> (direct Checkout API); idempotency-key on retryable POSTs; webhook integrity via adyen_hmac_key HMAC
external_integrations.pattern: Concrete realization of metadata gap #7: a real external acquirer integration. Outbound server-to-server REST to the Adyen Checkout API (/paymentMethods, /payments, /payments/details, /payments/{ref}/captures|cancels|refunds) authenticated with an X-API-Key; a parallel client-side Adyen Web drop-in/Components channel keyed by client_key; and inbound settlement via an HMAC-signature-verified webhook plus a redirect-return route handling 3DS1. The base 'payment' engine flags uses_api_keys but ships no live acquirer -- this module is exactly that override.
external_integrations.note: Prime gap-#7 example: none of the Adyen endpoints, the X-API-Key auth, the webhook HMAC trust, or the browser drop-in channel are derivable from Python model/field metadata; they were established only by reading models/payment_provider.py + payment_transaction.py + controllers/main.py.

Redirect-3DS handoff: 3DS1 / redirect-only method -> Adyen-hosted page -> /payment/adyen/return -> /payments/details -> _process -> /payment/status

classification.apqc_category: 9.0 Manage Financial Resources (9.5 process payments / collect cash; manage external payment provider)
classification.rationale: payment_adyen is a value-NETWORK (Stabell & Fjeldstad mediating-technology) component: a concrete acquirer adapter whose purpose is to interconnect two parties who would not otherwise transact directly -- the cardholder/payer and the merchant -- by linking the merchant to Adyen's card network. It exhibits the mediating-technology activities: network promotion & contract management (merchant-account/API-key/HMAC-key configuration and the per-amount/country drop-in payment-method discovery), service provisioning (creating the /payments charge and confirming it, with 3DS, per transaction), and infrastructure operation (the server-to-server Adyen Checkout API link, the Adyen Web drop-in client channel, and the HMAC-signed-webhook settlement loop). It does not transform inputs into outputs (chain) nor solve a bespoke customer problem (shop). It inherits the parent 'payment' engine's value_model exactly: the engine is the generic mediator and this module is its Adyen realization. activity_class is 'support' because, from the enterprise value-chain perspective, payment acceptance is an infrastructure/finance support function (category Accounting/Payment Providers, application=False, no end-user app) sitting under 9.0 Manage Financial Resources -- specifically 9.5 process payments / collect cash, with the side of 'manage an external payment provider'. So value_model=network (its own internal logic is mediation, an acquirer integration -- gap #7), activity_class=support (its place on the enterprise value chain). This mirrors the sibling payment_stripe.metamodel.json (network/support) and contrasts with account_payment (support/support), whose own logic is ledger record-keeping rather than mediation.

standard_capabilities: direct card payment via the Adyen Web drop-in (/paymentMethods + /payments), with SCA/3DS2 native and 3DS1 redirect handled by Adyen
tokenization / saved cards (Adyen stored payment method + shopperReference), including off-session recurring (ContAuth, recurringProcessingModel Subscription)
manual capture including partial capture, void, and partial refunds (support_manual_capture='partial', support_refund='partial')
multi payment-method support (methods queried per amount/country/locale from Adyen)
asynchronous settlement via an HMAC-signature-verified webhook plus a redirect-return confirmation route
typical_fits: online shop / portal checkout collecting card and local payments through Adyen across Europe and the US
save-card-for-later and tokenized recurring/subscription charges (off-session stored-PM /payments)
send-a-payment-link or pay-an-invoice-online collection (with account_payment / sale downstream)
merchants with an existing Adyen merchant account configuring credentials (merchant account, API key, client key, HMAC key, API URL prefix) directly
common_gaps: no self-onboarding flow: the merchant must obtain an Adyen merchant account and manually enter the merchant account / API key / client key / HMAC key / API URL prefix
the webhook (/payment/adyen/notification) needs a public URL and a correctly configured HMAC key registered in the Adyen Customer Area; a missing/invalid signature is rejected (403)
API endpoint version is keyed per-endpoint in const.API_ENDPOINT_VERSIONS -- newer Adyen API features/payment methods may need code changes
the set of default payment-method codes (const.DEFAULT_PAYMENT_METHOD_CODES) and method mapping (const.PAYMENT_METHODS_MAPPING) bound what is offered out of the box
bespoke reconciliation / settlement document chains live downstream (account_payment, sale), not here
